channel.title: Space Digest
channel.description: The podcasts worth your week, in a minute each.

item.title: The Next Era of Games: Mods, Agents, and Infinite Worlds
item.description: AI could turn games from fixed products into worlds players build, remix, and reshape while playing.

item.title: #356 Joe Kent - Susie Wiles, Stephen Miller, Midterms and the AIPAC Problem
item.description: The episode argues that voters did not abandon Trump—they felt betrayed by wars, lobbyists, and broken promises.

item.title: #2580 - Kenneth Lacovera
item.description: The fossil record reveals a world where dinosaurs ruled for ages, vanished almost instantly, and still shape science today.

item.title: What the Internet Boom Teaches Us About the AI Buildout | Mike Volpi
item.description: AI may be more valuable than the internet—but its boom could still end with fewer winners.

item.title: Wall Street Has No Idea What Anthropic Is Worth
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO may be worth $1.4 trillion, but the market is guessing because almost nobody knows what the company is worth.

item.title: King's Advisor Reveals What the Royal Family Knows About UFOs
item.description: Royal insiders, alleged crash recoveries, psychic encounters, and nuclear shutdowns form a deeply unsettling case for UFO secrecy.

item.title: JRE MMA Show #188 with Paddy Pimblett
item.description: Fighters may gain 35 pounds overnight, start camps at cave raves, and still question whether their best wins would hold today.

item.title: HubSpot’s Co-Founder on Finding Your Next Startup Idea
item.description: The best startup ideas may come from testing fast, solving ignored problems, and knowing when not to use AI.

item.title: Fable 5.2 Is the Best AI Ever. So Why Am I Not Switching Yet?
item.description: Fable 5.2 may be the strongest AI yet, but its biggest weakness is knowing what people actually want.

item.title: #2579 - Gary Sinise
item.description: Supporting veterans, Gary Sinise argues, means standing with people even when you oppose the wars they fought.

item.title: Scott Kupor on Building a16z and Rebuilding the Federal Workforce
item.description: A venture firm built its edge by turning one investor’s job into an entire support system—and government may need the same overhaul.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Admits Affair With Suspected Chinese Spy
item.description: Nvidia’s CEO says he cheated; the bigger question is whether China gained leverage over America’s most important AI company.

item.title: Marian Dogmas, The SSPX, and Leaving Atheism (Ethan Muse) | Ep. 604
item.description: Miracles, Marian doctrine, conversion, the SSPX, and Mormon origins are tied together by one test: authority.

item.title: #355 Captain Royce Williams - 101-Year-Old WWII Veteran & Medal of Honor Recipient
item.description: A pilot secretly fought six MiGs alone, survived a crippled jet, and waited decades for the truth to emerge.

item.title: 325. Stop Pushing Through: A Better Way to Handle Hard Work
item.description: Hard work gets better when you stop forcing the task and renew the purpose behind it.

item.title: The Health Interventions Actually Worth Your Time | Justin Mares
item.description: Most health advice gets lost in optimization; Justin Mares argues that a few boring habits matter more.

item.title: Agentic Video Is Real and Here’s What You Should Try
item.description: AI video is moving from a specialist craft to an everyday workplace tool—and the biggest gains may come after filming.

item.title: Mark Hyman’s Guide to Living Longer and Staying Strong
item.description: Longer life may depend less on extreme hacks than on building and keeping muscle.

item.title: Companies Are Spending 5x More on AI Now
item.description: AI spending is not slowing down—it is exploding because companies are paying for work, not employee seats.

item.title: Japan’s Defense Minister: “We Can’t Rule Out ALIENS!”
item.description: Japanese officials treat UFO reports near nuclear sites and alleged alien encounters as serious enough to investigate publicly.

item.title: Inside Salesforce’s $100 Billion M&A Playbook | John Somorjai
item.description: Salesforce’s acquisition edge is less about buying big companies than spotting talent, moving fast, and using its massive distribution.

item.title: #2578 - Calley Means
item.description: The episode argues that lobbyists, not voters, are quietly deciding which health reforms can survive Washington.

item.title: Why a Data Center Slowdown Benefits Big Tech
item.description: A slower data-center buildout could boost Big Tech by easing costs, raising margins, and letting the AI bubble deflate safely.

item.title: The New CFO: How AI Is Rewriting the Finance Function | Figma CFO Praveer Melwani
item.description: AI may shrink finance teams—but only after it makes their judgment more valuable.

item.title: Responding to Unhinged Women | Dr. Carrie Gress | Last Call Ep. 39
item.description: The episode argues that feminism turns women’s real struggles into contempt for men, victimhood, and rejection of family and faith.

item.title: #354 Reckless Ben - The Internet's Most Controversial Investigative YouTuber
item.description: A homeless stunt creator infiltrated cults, exposed abusive schools, and fought a religion in court without a lawyer.

item.title: #2577 - Gregory Forth
item.description: A 700,000-year-old human relative may have left behind living memories on Flores.

item.title: The New AI Agents That Shop, Plan, and Gossip
item.description: AI agents may become a society of helpers, friends, negotiators, and unpredictable digital characters.

item.title: How the Midterm Results Change AI
item.description: The election did not stop AI, but it made data centers a political liability that developers can no longer ignore.

item.title: #2576 - Dr. Peter McCullough
item.description: The episode argues that pandemic science was bent by money, fear, censorship, and a single-minded push for mass vaccination.

item.title: Andrew Huberman’s Three Rules for Better Health and Focus
item.description: Better health may come less from perfect routines than from a few repeatable habits that fit your real life.

item.title: AI Lurches Toward Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: AI may be starting to improve AI, but the bigger surprise is how little that guarantees about adoption or profits.

item.title: #2575 - Sam Tallent
item.description: A conversation about comedy, books, and mortality ends with the claim that AI may already be a new form of life.

item.title: The Robots Already Working in American Factories | Tutor Intelligence
item.description: Robots are already doing everyday factory work, but the hardest part is teaching them to handle reality.

item.title: How to Deslopify Your AI
item.description: AI makes publishing effortless, but the episode argues that human judgment—not speed—will decide what deserves attention.

item.title: Feminism is Dying (Thank God!) (Dr. Carrie Gress) | Ep. 603
item.description: Feminism, they argue, promised freedom but often leaves women angry, isolated, and far from the lives they wanted.

item.title: #353 Dr. Thomas Madden - Rome Historian Reveals the 7 Warning Signs of a Dying Republic
item.description: Rome’s republic did not collapse in one blow; it weakened as wealth, fear, and private armies replaced civic loyalty.

item.title: 324. Why Better Focus Starts With Meaning
item.description: Better focus does not begin with forcing attention; it begins with giving the work a reason to matter.

item.title: How Bending Spoons Built a $20 Billion Compounder | Luca Ferrari
item.description: Bending Spoons argues that steady improvements and disciplined acquisitions can beat rare flashes of genius.

item.title: AI Won’t Make Our Minds Useless According to 400 Years of History
item.description: AI may make human minds more valuable by freeing people to explore desires they never had time to pursue.

item.title: The Most Controversial Biologist Alive Breaks Down Telepathy
item.description: A controversial biologist argues that minds, animals, plants, and even stars may share fields of memory and awareness.

item.title: Can AI Fix Professional Networking? | Inside Cosign
item.description: Cosign wants AI agents to turn trusted recommendations into career connections, replacing cold applications with better-timed introductions.

item.title: #2574 - Francis Foster & Konstantin Kisin
item.description: From Iran and the Sphinx to universal income, the conversation keeps asking whether today’s certainties survive closer inspection.

item.title: Why AI Could Turn Small Law Firms Into Billion-Dollar Businesses
item.description: AI could make thousands of ignored legal claims profitable—and turn small firms into national businesses.

item.title: How the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Works
item.description: Spawn runs much of its company through persistent AI agents—and lets them break production to improve faster.

item.title: #2573 - Legion of Skanks
item.description: The episode jumps from organ transplants to self-driving cars, showing how ordinary life repeatedly turns bizarre.

item.title: The Startups Rebuilding American Industry | The AD50
item.description: America’s industrial comeback may depend less on new inventions than on building the factories to make them real.

item.title: The AI Rankings Just Got Reshuffled
item.description: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon takes the top AI ranking, while the new scoreboard sharply widens the gap between leading and open models.

item.title: 6 Myths About Porn | Jay Stringer | Last Call Ep. 38
item.description: Pornography does more than satisfy desire: it can teach, soothe, and expose the parts of life we have not learned to build.

item.title: #352 Cain Velasquez - UFC Champion Hunted the Man Accused of Abusing His 4-Year-Old Son
item.description: A UFC champion’s revenge, grief, and prison time pushed him toward a radically spiritual view of life.
